lines: {"concept_id": "drv.motion.region_entry", "kind": "formula", "contract": "The road user's footprint comes to overlap a structure region at the observation: it overlaps the region at the observation and did not overlap it at the observation before. The concept is the event of that coming to overlap, read at the observation at which the overlap has begun, and not the state of lying inside the region afterwards. It states no direction of entry, no carrier the road user came through, no speed and no place within the region. Not a stand-in for: lying within the region, which the occupancy relation carries on its own; a later observation at which the road user is still inside; the carrier or the way the road user came from, which a caller reads with its own relations; a crossing of a boundary the source represents by no region; or a leaving of the region.", "definition": null, "args": [{"name": "u", "sort": "track"}, {"name": "r", "sort": "region"}], "params": [], "elements": [{"span": "comes to overlap a structure region at the observation", "atoms": ["rel.occupies"], "concepts": [], "justification": "rel.occupies is 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, crosswalk, stop line, safety zone, bicycle lane, median, alley, curb zone, controlled-access lane, structure)', which is exactly the overlap of the footprint with the region argument at the observation; the kind of the region is the caller's, since the formal is a region variable the caller binds."}, {"span": "did not overlap it at the observation before", "atoms": ["rel.occupies"], "concepts": [], "justification": "the same relation read at the previous observation, which the formula language's 'rises' construct ('phi here and not at the previous observation') states over it; no other atom is read, so the event is the rise of that occupancy and nothing else."}], "residues": [], "literals": [], "scenarios": [{"name": "holds", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "A car's footprint is clear of the junction polygon at one scene and overlaps it at the next: the concept is true at that next scene."}, {"name": "fails", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "A car's footprint overlaps the junction polygon at both scenes: it is already inside, so the concept is false at the later scene."}, {"name": "blind", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "The source does not report whether the car's footprint overlaps the junction polygon at the earlier scene, so whether the overlap has just begun is unknown.", "masked": ["rel.occupies"]}], "used_by": ["NRS_484B_250_4_o1", "NRS_484B_250_4_o2", "NRS_484B_250_1", "NRS_484B_250_2", "NRS_484B_253_o1", "NRS_484B_253_o2", "NRS_484B_257_1_o1", "NRS_484B_257_1_o2", "NRS_484B_257_2_o1", "NRS_484B_257_2_o2", "NRS_484B_307_6a"], "supersedes": null}

{"node_id": "NRS_484B_250_4_o1", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-250-4"], "subject": {"binder": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "t1", "text": "When a vehicle enters an intersection controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered, but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,", "role": "trigger"}, {"id": "s1", "text": "the driver of the vehicle", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "ob1", "text": "shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.", "role": "obligation"}, {"id": "sib1", "text": "After making such a stop, the driver shall proceed cautiously, yielding to vehicles which have previously completed a stop or are within the intersection.", "role": "sibling"}], "elements": [{"span": "t1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle", "rel.occupies", "st.intersection", "dev.traffic_signal", "dev.governs", "dev.inoperative"], "derived": ["drv.motion.region_entry"], "justification": "'a vehicle' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except ...'), admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. 'enters an intersection' is the event drv.motion.region_entry denotes ('comes to overlap a structure region at the observation'), on a region of kind st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'); rel.occupies anchors the entry to the subject's own footprint ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') rather than any junction of the scene, and is the kind-ranging relation the region quantifier needs. 'controlled by' is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself', read on the same intersection the subject enters. 'but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection' is dev.inoperative, 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', read at the entry observation. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: the duty reads where the signal controls, not where a halt is due, and the halt's place is read in ob1 from its own marks. dev.traffic_signal is a device, not a sign, so no sign atom is claimed here. drv.motion.region_entry is not a stand-in for lying within the junction: the words fix the inoperative state to the instant of entry, so the entry event, not the occupancy, is what the condition is read at."}, {"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"], "derived": [], "justification": "'the driver of the vehicle' singles out no further road user: DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes 'driver' the person who drives or is in actual physical control of the vehicle, and the ontology's section on what is not an atom reads 'drives', 'operates' and 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds the vehicle whose entry t1 reads. The class is the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom and never expanded into the classes it covers; the mapping index maps 'The driver of a vehicle' to the same atom."}, {"span": "ob1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic", "rel.occupies", "st.stop_line", "st.crosswalk", "st.entrance_of", "st.region_geometry", "st.travel_region", "st.lane_direction", "st.lane_enters", "st.intersection", "st.on_way", "st.highway", "st.sight_along_way", "prim.region_offset_along"], "derived": ["drv.motion.standstill"], "justification": "'shall stop' is the halt DEF-NRS-484A-255 defines, 'complete cessation from movement', which drv.motion.standstill carries with the speed tolerance its contract names. 'at a clearly marked stop line' is st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device'; st.entrance_of ties it to the subject's own approach, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks ... the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before', and st.lane_enters gives that carrier 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', so the line read is the one marking the entrance the subject enters by and never a line merely near it. st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over ('the union of the kinds a device can govern: a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection'), rel.occupies the anchor that makes it the subject's own carrier. 'before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection' is st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', again tied by st.entrance_of, with the near side read as the crossing marking that entrance. prim.region_offset_along gives the side the subject is on, 'the signed distance from a road user's reference point to a structure region, measured along a carrier's designated direction', with st.lane_direction the direction it is measured along, and st.region_geometry the distance between the subject's body and the mark ('the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'), which is what the stop-point tolerance bounds; the primitive's own inputs are not claimed beside it, and st.region_geometry is claimed for that distance, not for the primitive. 'at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway' is st.sight_along_way, 'the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye at the observation ... the smaller of the two directions', which is the view of traffic approaching on the crossing way from where the subject stands; st.on_way and st.highway bind that way ('the public way a structure region lies on'; 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'). 'approaching traffic' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-285 defines, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel', admitted as ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and claimed as one atom. st.sight_along_way is not a stand-in for whether an actual road user is seen (rel.visible): the words require a view of the way, whether or not anyone is on it, which is what this atom and not that relation carries. st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line, and the three places are read in the order the words give them."}], "operationalizations": [], "assumptions": [], "intentions": [], "compositions": [], "residues": [], "binders": [{"name": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}], "applicability": "The subject vehicle enters an intersection (its footprint comes to overlap the junction region at the observation) and, at that entry observation, a traffic-control signal governs that intersection, is installed with its vehicular faces uncovered, and is inoperative.", "obligation": "Before that entry the subject must have come to a complete halt at the place the words name, in their order. The event is the subject's entry into that intersection; the target is the approach carrier the subject occupies whose entrance end is that intersection. The place is the stop line recorded as marking that carrier; where the carrier's stop lines are observed and none marks it, the crosswalk recorded as marking that carrier; where neither is marked, the point on that carrier nearest the intersection at which the sight along the crossing way, in the lesser of its two directions, is at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance. The search for the halt runs back from the entry observation and ends at the start of that approach -- the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the mark marks, was off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance -- or at the previous entry of the same subject into the same intersection, and at nothing else: not at another junction, not at the first observation of the recording, not at a distance travelled. Where the search finds the halt the duty is met; where it reaches either end without it the duty is violated; where it reaches neither end, because the history the bound needs begins before the recording or because the carrier's association with the mark or the carrier's direction is not observed, the duty is unknown. No other road user is in the scene.", "masked": []}, {"name": "permit", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "The same junction and the same inoperative signal. The scene contains no other road user, and the verdict is still decided.", "masked": []}, {"name": "idle", "expected": "not_applicable", "narrative": "The same junction, but the signal governing it shows a steady circular red and is not inoperative. The car enters the junction without halting: the trigger does not hold, so the rule is not engaged.", "masked": []}, {"name": "blind", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "The car enters the junction without halting, the signal is installed and uncovered, but the source does not report whether the head is showing a valid indication, so whether it was inoperative at the entry is unknown and the rule reports unknown.", "masked": ["dev.inoperative"]}, {"name": "branch_1", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "A junction with the same inoperative signal where the lane's stop lines and crosswalks are observed and none marks the car's lane. lines: {"node_id": "NRS_484B_250_4_o1", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-250-4"], "subject": {"binder": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "t1", "text": "When a vehicle enters an intersection controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered, but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,", "role": "trigger"}, {"id": "s1", "text": "the driver of the vehicle", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "ob1", "text": "shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.", "role": "obligation"}, {"id": "sib1", "text": "After making such a stop, the driver shall proceed cautiously, yielding to vehicles which have previously completed a stop or are within the intersection.", "role": "sibling"}], "elements": [{"span": "t1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle", "rel.occupies", "st.intersection", "dev.traffic_signal", "dev.governs", "dev.inoperative"], "derived": ["drv.motion.region_entry"], "justification": "'a vehicle' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except ...'), admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. 'enters an intersection' is the event drv.motion.region_entry denotes ('comes to overlap a structure region at the observation'), on a region of kind st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'); rel.occupies anchors the entry to the subject's own footprint ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') rather than any junction of the scene, and is the kind-ranging relation the region quantifier needs. 'a traffic-control signal' is DEF-NRS-484A-290, 'any official traffic-control device, whether manually, electrically or mechanically operated, placed or erected by a public authority or railroad, by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed': dev.traffic_signal is 'a signal head' with states circular_green/circular_yellow/circular_red and the rest, the only device atom that alternately directs traffic to stop or proceed, and its 'uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered' carries 'which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered' word for word. 'controlled by' is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself', read on the same intersection the subject enters. 'but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection' is dev.inoperative, 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', read at the entry observation. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: the duty reads where the signal controls, not where a halt is due, and the halt's place is read in ob1 from its own marks. dev.traffic_signal is a device, not a sign, so no sign atom is claimed here. drv.motion.region_entry is not a stand-in for lying within the junction: the words fix the inoperative state to the instant of entry, so the entry event, not the occupancy, is what the condition is read at."}, {"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"], "derived": [], "justification": "'the driver of the vehicle' singles out no further road user: DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes 'driver' the person who drives or is in actual physical control of the vehicle, and the ontology's section on what is not an atom reads 'drives', 'operates' and 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds the vehicle whose entry t1 reads. The class is the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom and never expanded into the classes it covers; the mapping index maps 'The driver of a vehicle' to the same atom."}, {"span": "ob1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic", "rel.occupies", "st.stop_line", "st.crosswalk", "st.entrance_of", "st.region_geometry", "st.travel_region", "st.lane_direction", "st.lane_enters", "st.intersection", "st.on_way", "st.highway", "st.sight_along_way", "prim.region_offset_along"], "derived": ["drv.motion.standstill"], "justification": "'shall stop' is the halt DEF-NRS-484A-255 defines, 'complete cessation from movement', which drv.motion.standstill carries with the speed tolerance its contract names. 'at a clearly marked stop line' is st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device'; st.entrance_of ties it to the subject's own approach, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks ... the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before', and st.lane_enters gives that carrier 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', so the line read is the one marking the entrance the subject enters by and never a line merely near it. st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over ('the union of the kinds a device can govern: a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection'), rel.occupies the anchor that makes it the subject's own carrier. 'before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection' is st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', again tied by st.entrance_of, with the near side read as the crossing marking that entrance. prim.region_offset_along gives the side the subject is on, 'the signed distance from a road user's reference point to a structure region, measured along a carrier's designated direction', with st.lane_direction the direction it is measured along, and st.region_geometry the distance between the subject's body and the mark ('the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'), which is what the stop-point tolerance bounds; the primitive's own inputs are not claimed beside it, and st.region_geometry is claimed for that distance, not for the primitive. 'at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway' is st.sight_along_way, 'the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye at the observation ... the smaller of the two directions', which is the view of traffic approaching on the crossing way from where the subject stands; st.on_way and st.highway bind that way ('the public way a structure region lies on'; 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'). 'approaching traffic' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-285 defines, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel', admitted as ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and claimed as one atom. st.sight_along_way is not a stand-in for whether an actual road user is seen (rel.visible): the words require a view of the way, whether or not anyone is on it, which is what this atom and not that relation carries. st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line, and the three places are read in the order the words give them."}], "operationalizations": [], "assumptions": [], "intentions": [], "compositions": [], "residues": [], "binders": [{"name": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}], "applicability": "The subject vehicle enters an intersection (its footprint comes to overlap the junction region at the observation) and, at that entry observation, a traffic-control signal governs that intersection, is installed with its vehicular faces uncovered, and is inoperative.", "obligation": "Before that entry the subject must have come to a complete halt at the place the words name, in their order. The event is the subject's entry into that intersection; the target is the approach carrier the subject occupies whose entrance end is that intersection. The place is the stop line recorded as marking that carrier; where the carrier's stop lines are observed and none marks it, the crosswalk recorded as marking that carrier; where neither is marked, the point on that carrier nearest the intersection at which the sight along the crossing way, in the lesser of its two directions, is at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance. A halt counts at the place when the subject's speed is at or below p.standstill_speed_tolerance while the distance between its body and the mark is at most p.stop_point_tolerance and it has not yet passed the mark, the side being read by the sign of prim.region_offset_along along the carrier's designated direction; a halt whose footprint already overlaps the intersection is not at the place. The search for the halt runs back from the entry observation and ends at the start of that approach -- the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the mark marks, was off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance -- or at the previous entry of the same subject into the same intersection, and at nothing else: not at another junction, not at the first observation of the recording, not at a distance travelled. Where the search finds the halt the duty is met; where it reaches either end without it the duty is violated; where it reaches neither end, because the history the bound needs begins before the recording or because the carrier's association with the mark or the carrier's direction is not observed, the duty is unknown. Where the stop line's entrances are observed and exclude the subject's carrier, the place is read from the next words in order and the duty is not unknown on that ground.", "params": ["p.standstill_speed_tolerance", "p.stop_point_tolerance", "p.intersecting_way_view_distance"], "narrowings": [{"span": "ob1", "why": "'shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection' is read through the conduct the same sentence and the next one prescribe -- the halt at the place and, in the second node, the cautious proceeding with its yielding -- and not through a stop-sign device: no stop sign is present in the scene, and reading one in would make the rule turn on a device the trace does not show.", "kind": "reading"}, {"span": "ob1", "why": "'a clearly marked stop line' is read as the stop line the scene represents: the line's presence is the evidence of its clear marking, and the paint's clarity or wear is not modelled. The reading relaxes neither which place governs nor the halt and its timing.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "status"}, {"span": "ob1", "why": "'the through highway' is read as the highway the subject's approach crosses at that intersection: DEF-NRS-484A-275 makes a through highway one at whose entrances traffic is required by law to yield in obedience to a stop sign, a yield sign or other device, which is a legal designation no feature of a scene with an inoperative signal displays; the words' purpose here is the view of the traffic the subject must give way to, and that traffic approaches on the crossing way.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "status"}, {"span": "ob1", "why": "'has a view of approaching traffic' is read as the sight along the crossing way reaching at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance in the lesser of its two directions, and not as the driver's actual perception, which no trace carries.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "perception"}, {"span": "s1", "why": "'the driver of the vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "agency"}], "scenarios": [{"name": "forbid", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "A car approaches a four-way junction whose signal heads are installed, uncovered and dark with no valid indication. A stop line is recorded as marking the lane the car occupies, the lane's entrance end is that junction, and the car crosses the line and enters the junction without its speed ever falling to the standstill tolerance anywhere on the approach from the line's upstream zone onward. No other road user is in the scene.", "masked": []}, {"name": "permit", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "The same junction and the same inoperative signal. The car halts with its speed at zero while its body is within the stop-point tolerance of the stop line marking its lane and short of the line, then moves off and enters the junction. The scene contains no other road user, and the verdict is still decided.", "masked": []}, {"name": "idle", "expected": "not_applicable", "narrative": "The same junction, but the signal governing it shows a steady circular red and is not inoperative. The car enters the junction without halting: the trigger does not hold, so the rule is not engaged.", "masked": []}, {"name": "blind", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "The car enters the junction without halting, the signal is installed and uncovered, but the source does not report whether the head is showing a valid indication, so whether it was inoperative at the entry is unknown and the rule reports unknown.", "masked": ["dev.inoperative"]}, {"name": "branch_1", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "A junction with the same inoperative signal where the lane's stop lines and crosswalks are observed and none marks the car's lane. The car halts, with its speed at zero, on its lane at the point nearest the junction at which the sight along the crossing way reaches the view distance, then enters: the third place in the words' order governs and the duty is met.", "masked": []}, {"name": "branch_2", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "The same junction and inoperative signal, with no stop line but a marked crosswalk recorded as marking the car's lane. The car slows to a crawl above the standstill tolerance before the crosswalk and rolls into the junction: the second place in the words' order governs and no halt is found on the approach.", "masked": []}, {"name": "history_boundary", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "The recording begins with the car already between the stop line and the junction, inside the line's stopping zone, and the car then enters the junction while the signal is inoperative. No halt is recorded, and the recording contains neither the start of the approach upstream of the line nor a previous entry of the car into that junction, so no recorded act and no visible end of the search decides the verdict.", "boundary": "the stretch of the approach upstream of the stop line's stopping zone, at which the car entered that zone, lies before the first observation of the recording"}], "literals": [], "param_proposals": [], "gaps": []}

lines: {"concept_id": "drv.motion.region_entry", "kind": "formula", "contract": "The road user's footprint comes to overlap a structure region at the observation: it overlaps the region at the observation and did not overlap it at the observation before. The concept is the event of that coming to overlap, read at the observation at which the overlap has begun, and not the state of lying inside the region afterwards. It states no direction of entry, no carrier the road user came through, no speed and no place within the region. Not a stand-in for: lying within the region, which the occupancy relation carries on its own; a later observation at which the road user is still inside; the carrier or the way the road user came from, which a caller reads with its own relations; a crossing of a boundary the source represents by no region; or a leaving of the region.", "definition": null, "args": [{"name": "u", "sort": "track"}, {"name": "r", "sort": "region"}], "params": [], "elements": [{"span": "comes to overlap a structure region at the observation", "atoms": ["rel.occupies"], "concepts": [], "justification": "rel.occupies is 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, crosswalk, stop line, safety zone, bicycle lane, median, alley, curb zone, controlled-access lane, structure)', which is exactly the overlap of the footprint with the region argument at the observation; the kind of the region is the caller's, since the formal is a region variable the caller binds."}, {"span": "did not overlap it at the observation before", "atoms": ["rel.occupies"], "concepts": [], "justification": "the same relation read at the previous observation, which the formula language's 'rises' construct ('phi here and not at the previous observation') states over it; no other atom is read, so the event is the rise of that occupancy and nothing else."}], "residues": [], "literals": [], "scenarios": [{"name": "holds", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "A car's footprint is clear of the junction polygon at one scene and overlaps it at the next: the concept is true at that next scene."}, {"name": "fails", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "A car's footprint overlaps the junction polygon at both scenes: it is already inside, so the concept is false at the later scene."}, {"name": "blind", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "The source does not report whether the car's footprint overlaps the junction polygon at the earlier scene, so whether the overlap has just begun is unknown.", "masked": ["rel.occupies"]}], "used_by": ["NRS_484B_250_4_o1", "NRS_484B_250_4_o2", "NRS_484B_250_1", "NRS_484B_250_2", "NRS_484B_253_o1", "NRS_484B_253_o2", "NRS_484B_257_1_o1", "NRS_484B_257_1_o2", "NRS_484B_257_2_o1", "NRS_484B_257_2_o2", "NRS_484B_307_6a"], "supersedes": null}

{"node_id": "NRS_484B_250_4_o1", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-250-4"], "subject": {"binder": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "t1", "text": "When a vehicle enters an intersection controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered, but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,", "role": "trigger"}, {"id": "s1", "text": "the driver of the vehicle", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "ob1", "text": "shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.", "role": "obligation"}, {"id": "sib1", "text": "After making such a stop, the driver shall proceed cautiously, yielding to vehicles which have previously completed a stop or are within the intersection.", "role": "sibling"}], "elements": [{"span": "t1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle", "rel.occupies", "st.intersection", "dev.traffic_signal", "dev.governs", "dev.inoperative"], "derived": ["drv.motion.region_entry"], "justification": "'a vehicle' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except ...'), admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. 'enters an intersection' is the event drv.motion.region_entry denotes ('comes to overlap a structure region at the observation'), on a region of kind st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'); rel.occupies anchors the entry to the subject's own footprint ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') rather than any junction of the scene, and is the kind-ranging relation the region quantifier needs. 'a traffic-control signal' is DEF-NRS-484A-290, 'any official traffic-control device, whether manually, electrically or mechanically operated, placed or erected by a public authority or railroad, by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed': dev.traffic_signal is 'a signal head' with states circular_green/circular_yellow/circular_red and the rest, the only device atom that alternately directs traffic to stop or proceed, and its 'uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered' carries 'which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered' word for word. 'controlled by' is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself', read on the same intersection the subject enters. 'but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection' is dev.inoperative, 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', read at the entry observation. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: the duty reads where the signal controls, not where a halt is due, and the halt's place is read in ob1 from its own marks. dev.traffic_signal is a device, not a sign, so no sign atom is claimed here. drv.motion.region_entry is not a stand-in for lying within the junction: the words fix the inoperative state to the instant of entry, so the entry event, not the occupancy, is what the condition is read at."}, {"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"], "derived": [], "justification": "'the driver of the vehicle' singles out no further road user: DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes 'driver' the person who drives or is in actual physical control of the vehicle, and the ontology's section on what is not an atom reads 'drives', 'operates' and 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds the vehicle whose entry t1 reads. 'at a clearly marked stop line' is st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device'; st.entrance_of ties it to the subject's own approach, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks ... the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before', and st.lane_enters gives that carrier 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', so the line read is the one marking the entrance the subject enters by and never a line merely near it. st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over ('the union of the kinds a device can govern: a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection'), rel.occupies the anchor that makes it the subject's own carrier. lines: {"concept_id": "drv.motion.region_entry", "kind": "formula", "contract": "The road user's footprint comes to overlap a structure region at the observation: it overlaps the region at the observation and did not overlap it at the observation before. The concept is the event of that coming to overlap, read at the observation at which the overlap has begun, and not the state of lying inside the region afterwards. It states no direction of entry, no carrier the road user came through, no speed and no place within the region. Not a stand-in for: lying within the region, which the occupancy relation carries on its own; a later observation at which the road user is still inside; the carrier or the way the road user came from, which a caller reads with its own relations; a crossing of a boundary the source represents by no region; or a leaving of the region.", "definition": null, "args": [{"name": "u", "sort": "track"}, {"name": "r", "sort": "region"}], "params": [], "elements": [{"span": "comes to overlap a structure region at the observation", "atoms": ["rel.occupies"], "concepts": [], "justification": "rel.occupies is 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, crosswalk, stop line, safety zone, bicycle lane, median, alley, curb zone, controlled-access lane, structure)', which is exactly the overlap of the footprint with the region argument at the observation; the kind of the region is the caller's, since the formal is a region variable the caller binds."}, {"span": "did not overlap it at the observation before", "atoms": ["rel.occupies"], "concepts": [], "justification": "the same relation read at the previous observation, which the formula language's 'rises' construct ('phi here and not at the previous observation') states over it; no other atom is read, so the event is the rise of that occupancy and nothing else."}], "residues": [], "literals": [], "scenarios": [{"name": "holds", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "A car's footprint is clear of the junction polygon at one scene and overlaps it at the next: the concept is true at that next scene."}, {"name": "fails", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "A car's footprint overlaps the junction polygon at both scenes: it is already inside, so the concept is false at the later scene."}, {"name": "blind", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "The source does not report whether the car's footprint overlaps the junction polygon at the earlier scene, so whether the overlap has just begun is unknown.", "masked": ["rel.occupies"]}], "used_by": ["NRS_484B_250_4_o1", "NRS_484B_250_4_o2", "NRS_484B_250_1", "NRS_484B_250_2", "NRS_484B_253_o1", "NRS_484B_253_o2", "NRS_484B_257_1_o1", "NRS_484B_257_1_o2", "NRS_484B_257_2_o1", "NRS_484B_257_2_o2", "NRS_484B_307_6a"], "supersedes": null}

{"node_id": "NRS_484B_250_4_o1", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-250-4"], "subject": {"binder": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "t1", "text": "When a vehicle enters an intersection controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered, but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,", "role": "trigger"}, {"id": "s1", "text": "the driver of the vehicle", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "ob1", "text": "shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.", "role": "obligation"}, {"id": "sib1", "text": "After making such a stop, the driver shall proceed cautiously, yielding to vehicles which have previously completed a stop or are within the intersection.", "role": "sibling"}], "elements": [{"span": "t1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle", "rel.occupies", "st.intersection", "dev.traffic_signal", "dev.governs", "dev.inoperative"], "derived": ["drv.motion.region_entry"], "justification": "'a vehicle' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except ...'), admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. 'enters an intersection' is the event drv.motion.region_entry denotes ('comes to overlap a structure region at the observation'), on a region of kind st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'); rel.occupies anchors the entry to the subject's own footprint ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') rather than any junction of the scene, and is the kind-ranging relation the region quantifier needs. 'controlled by' is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself', read on the same intersection the subject enters. 'but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection' is dev.inoperative, 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', read at the entry observation. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: the duty reads where the signal controls, not where a halt is due, and the halt's place is read in ob1 from its own marks. dev.traffic_signal is a device, not a sign, so no sign atom is claimed here. drv.motion.region_entry is not a stand-in for lying within the junction: the words fix the inoperative state to the instant of entry, so the entry event, not the occupancy, is what the condition is read at."}, {"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"], "derived": [], "justification": "'the driver of the vehicle' singles out no further road user: DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes 'driver' the person who drives or is in actual physical control of the vehicle, and the ontology's section on what is not an atom reads 'drives', 'operates' and 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds the vehicle whose entry t1 reads. 'at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway' is st.sight_along_way, 'the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye at the observation ... the smaller of the two directions', which is the view of traffic approaching on the crossing way from where the subject stands; st.on_way and st.highway bind that way ('the public way a structure region lies on'; 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'). The event is the subject's entry into that intersection; the target is the approach carrier the subject occupies whose entrance end is that intersection. The place is the stop line recorded as marking that carrier; where the carrier's stop lines are observed and none marks it, the crosswalk recorded as marking that carrier; where neither is marked, the point on that carrier nearest the intersection at which the sight along the crossing way, in the lesser of its two directions, is at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance. lines: {"node_id": "NRS_484B_250_4_o1", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-250-4"], "subject": {"binder": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "t1", "text": "When a vehicle enters an intersection controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered, but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,", "role": "trigger"}, {"id": "s1", "text": "the driver of the vehicle", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "ob1", "text": "shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.", "role": "obligation"}, {"id": "sib1", "text": "After making such a stop, the driver shall proceed cautiously, yielding to vehicles which have previously completed a stop or are within the intersection.", "role": "sibling"}], "elements": [{"span": "t1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle", "rel.occupies", "st.intersection", "dev.traffic_signal", "dev.governs", "dev.inoperative"], "derived": ["drv.motion.region_entry"], "justification": "'a vehicle' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except ...'), admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. 'enters an intersection' is the event drv.motion.region_entry denotes ('comes to overlap a structure region at the observation'), on a region of kind st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'); rel.occupies anchors the entry to the subject's own footprint ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') rather than any junction of the scene, and is the kind-ranging relation the region quantifier needs. 'a traffic-control signal' is DEF-NRS-484A-290, 'any official traffic-control device, whether manually, electrically or mechanically operated, placed or erected by a public authority or railroad, by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed': dev.traffic_signal is 'a signal head' with states circular_green/circular_yellow/circular_red and the rest, the only device atom that alternately directs traffic to stop or proceed, and its 'uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered' carries 'which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered' word for word. 'controlled by' is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself', read on the same intersection the subject enters. 'but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection' is dev.inoperative, 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', read at the entry observation. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: the duty reads where the signal controls, not where a halt is due, and the halt's place is read in ob1 from its own marks. dev.traffic_signal is a device, not a sign, so no sign atom is claimed here. drv.motion.region_entry is not a stand-in for lying within the junction: the words fix the inoperative state to the instant of entry, so the entry event, not the occupancy, is what the condition is read at."}, {"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"], "derived": [], "justification": "'the driver of the vehicle' singles out no further road user: DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes 'driver' the person who drives or is in actual physical control of the vehicle, and the ontology's section on what is not an atom reads 'drives', 'operates' and 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds the vehicle whose entry t1 reads. The class is the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom and never expanded into the classes it covers; the mapping index maps 'The driver of a vehicle' to the same atom."}, {"span": "ob1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic", "rel.occupies", "st.stop_line", "st.crosswalk", "st.entrance_of", "st.region_geometry", "st.travel_region", "st.lane_direction", "st.lane_enters", "st.intersection", "st.on_way", "st.highway", "st.sight_along_way", "prim.region_offset_along"], "derived": ["drv.motion.standstill"], "justification": "'shall stop' is the halt DEF-NRS-484A-255 defines, 'complete cessation from movement', which drv.motion.standstill carries with the speed tolerance its contract names. 'at a clearly marked stop line' is st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device'; st.entrance_of ties it to the subject's own approach, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks ... the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before', and st.lane_enters gives that carrier 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', so the line read is the one marking the entrance the subject enters by and never a line merely near it. st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over ('the union of the kinds a device can govern: a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection'), rel.occupies the anchor that makes it the subject's own carrier. 'before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection' is st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', again tied by st.entrance_of, with the near side read as the crossing marking that entrance. prim.region_offset_along gives the side the subject is on, 'the signed distance from a road user's reference point to a structure region, measured along a carrier's designated direction', with st.lane_direction the direction it is measured along, and st.region_geometry the distance between the subject's body and the mark ('the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'), which is what the stop-point tolerance bounds; the primitive's own inputs are not claimed beside it, and st.region_geometry is claimed for that distance, not for the primitive. 'at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway' is st.sight_along_way, 'the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye at the observation ... the smaller of the two directions', which is the view of traffic approaching on the crossing way from where the subject stands; st.on_way and st.highway bind that way ('the public way a structure region lies on'; 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'). 'approaching traffic' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-285 defines, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel', admitted as ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and claimed as one atom. st.sight_along_way is not a stand-in for whether an actual road user is seen (rel.visible): the words require a view of the way, whether or not anyone is on it, which is what this atom and not that relation carries. st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line, and the three places are read in the order the words give them."}], "operationalizations": [], "assumptions": [], "intentions": [], "compositions": [], "residues": [], "binders": [{"name": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}], "applicability": "The subject vehicle enters an intersection (its footprint comes to overlap the junction region at the observation) and, at that entry observation, a traffic-control signal governs that intersection, is installed with its vehicular faces uncovered, and is inoperative.", "obligation": "Before that entry the subject must have come to a complete halt at the place the words name, in their order. The event is the subject's entry into that intersection; the target is the approach carrier the subject occupies whose entrance end is that intersection. The place is the stop line recorded as marking that carrier; where the carrier's stop lines are observed and none marks it, the crosswalk recorded as marking that carrier; where neither is marked, the point on that carrier nearest the intersection at which the sight along the crossing way, in the lesser of its two directions, is at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance. A halt counts at the place when the subject's speed is at or below p.standstill_speed_tolerance while the distance between its body and the mark is at most p.stop_point_tolerance and it has not yet passed the mark, the side being read by the sign of prim.region_offset_along along the carrier's designated direction; a halt whose footprint already overlaps the intersection is not at the place. The search for the halt runs back from the entry observation and ends at the start of that approach -- the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the mark marks, was off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance -- or at the previous entry of the same subject into the same intersection, and at nothing else: not at another junction, not at the first observation of the recording, not at a distance travelled. Where the search finds the halt the duty is met; where it reaches either end without it the duty is violated; where it reaches neither end, because the history the bound needs begins before the recording or because the carrier's association with the mark or the carrier's direction is not observed, the duty is unknown. Where the stop line's entrances are observed and exclude the subject's carrier, the place is read from the next words in order and the duty is not unknown on that ground.", "params": ["p.standstill_speed_tolerance", "p.stop_point_tolerance", "p.intersecting_way_view_distance"], "narrowings": [{"span": "ob1", "why": "'shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection' is read through the conduct the same sentence and the next one prescribe -- the halt at the place and, in the second node, the cautious proceeding with its yielding -- and not through a stop-sign device: no stop sign is present in the scene, and reading one in would make the rule turn on a device the trace does not show.", "kind": "reading"}, {"span": "ob1", "why": "'a clearly marked stop line' is read as the stop line the scene represents: the line's presence is the evidence of its clear marking, and the paint's clarity or wear is not modelled. The reading relaxes neither which place governs nor the halt and its timing.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "status"}, {"span": "ob1", "why": "'the through highway' is read as the highway the subject's approach crosses at that intersection: DEF-NRS-484A-275 makes a through highway one at whose entrances traffic is required by law to yield in obedience to a stop sign, a yield sign or other device, which is a legal designation no feature of a scene with an inoperative signal displays; the words' purpose here is the view of the traffic the subject must give way to, and that traffic approaches on the crossing way.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "status"}, {"span": "ob1", "why": "'has a view of approaching traffic' is read as the sight along the crossing way reaching at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance in the lesser of its two directions, and not as the driver's actual perception, which no trace carries.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "perception"}, {"span": "s1", "why": "'the driver of the vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "agency"}], "scenarios": [{"name": "forbid", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "A car approaches a four-way junction whose signal heads are installed, uncovered and dark with no valid indication. A stop line is recorded as marking the lane the car occupies, the lane's entrance end is that junction, and the car crosses the line and enters the junction without its speed ever falling to the standstill tolerance anywhere on the approach from the line's upstream zone onward. No other road user is in the scene.", "masked": []}, {"name": "permit", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "The same junction and the same inoperative signal. The car halts with its speed at zero while its body is within the stop-point tolerance of the stop line marking its lane and short of the line, then moves off and enters the junction. The scene contains no other road user, and the verdict is still decided.", "masked": []}, {"name": "idle", "expected": "not_applicable", "narrative": "The same junction, but the signal governing it shows a steady circular red and is not inoperative. The car enters the junction without halting: the trigger does not hold, so the rule is not engaged.", "masked": []}, {"name": "blind", "expected": "unknown", "narrative": "The car enters the junction without halting, the signal is installed and uncovered, but the source does not report whether the head is showing a valid indication, so whether it was inoperative at the entry is unknown and the rule reports unknown.", "masked": ["dev.inoperative"]}, {"name": "branch_1", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "A junction with the same inoperative signal where the lane's stop lines and crosswalks are observed and none marks the car's lane. The car halts, with its speed at zero, on its lane at the point nearest the junction at which the sight along the crossing way reaches the view distance, then enters: the third place in the words' order governs and the duty is met.", "masked": []}, {"name": "branch_2", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "The same junction and inoperative signal, with no stop line but a marked crosswalk recorded as marking the car's lane. lines: {"node_id": "NRS_484B_250_1", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-250-1"], "subject": {"binder": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "s1", "text": "The driver of a vehicle", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "t1", "text": "approaching an intersection", "role": "trigger"}, {"id": "ob1", "text": "shall yield the right-of-way to a vehicle which has entered the intersection from a different highway.", "role": "obligation"}, {"id": "r1", "text": "Except as otherwise provided in subsection 4 [NRS-484B-250-4],", "role": "reference"}, {"id": "e1", "text": "this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices", "role": "exception"}, {"id": "e2", "text": "or to vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions,", "role": "exception"}, {"id": "e3", "text": "when the driver of one of the vehicles is intending to", "role": "exception"}, {"id": "e4", "text": "or is making a left turn.", "role": "exception"}], "elements": [{"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"], "derived": [], "justification": "'The driver of a vehicle' names no road user beyond the vehicle: DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes the driver the person who drives or is in actual physical control of it, and the ontology reads 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds that vehicle. Its class is the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except ...'), claimed as one atom and never expanded; the mapping index maps the same words to the same atom."}, {"span": "t1", "atoms": ["rel.occupies", "st.travel_region", "st.lane_enters", "st.intersection"], "derived": [], "justification": "The ontology fixes what approaching an intersection is: 'a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection (st.lane_enters)'. st.lane_enters is 'the relation: the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over ('a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection'), st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges') the junction itself, and rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') the anchor that makes the carrier the subject's own. lines: {"node_id": "NRS_484B_257_1_o1", "law_refs": ["NRS-484B-257-1"], "subject": {"binder": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}, "segmentation": [{"id": "e1", "text": "Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal:", "role": "exception"}, {"id": "c1", "text": "When proper signs have been erected,", "role": "condition"}, {"id": "s1", "text": "the driver of a vehicle", "role": "subject"}, {"id": "ob1", "text": "shall stop or yield at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, then at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.", "role": "obligation"}, {"id": "sib1", "text": "After having stopped or, in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped, the driver shall yield the right-of-way to other vehicles which have entered the intersection from such through highway or which are approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.", "role": "sibling"}], "elements": [{"span": "e1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic", "dev.human_direction", "dev.traffic_signal", "dev.governs", "rel.occupies", "st.travel_region", "st.lane_enters", "st.intersection"], "derived": [], "justification": "'traffic' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-285 defines, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel', admitted as the aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and claimed as one atom. 'being controlled by a police officer' is dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role is police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger; indication is stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)', read with role police_officer, which is DEF-NRS-484A-180's 'officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic'; the atom carries the direction given, so a person present but directing nothing does not engage the exception. 'or a traffic-control signal' is dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head', the device by which traffic is 'alternately directed to stop or proceed' as DEF-NRS-484A-290 requires. The controlling is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection', read on the junction the subject approaches or on its own approach carrier, which rel.occupies, st.travel_region, st.lane_enters and st.intersection bind to the subject's own approach, so that a signal governing another junction of the scene does not excuse the duty. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position, and no halt place is read from it."}, {"span": "c1", "atoms": ["dev.stop_sign", "dev.yield_sign", "dev.governs", "rel.occupies", "st.travel_region", "st.lane_enters", "st.intersection"], "derived": [], "justification": "'proper signs' are, in this section, the stop sign and the yield sign its own words name: dev.stop_sign is the 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt' and dev.yield_sign the 'regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt'. 'have been erected' is read as the sign's presence on the road governing the subject's approach: dev.governs gives 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', read on the carrier the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) whose entrance end is the junction (st.lane_enters, st.intersection), so the sign read is the one governing this approach and not any sign of the scene. Which of the two signs governs decides which act the obligation owes."}, {"span": "s1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"], "derived": [], "justification": "'the driver of a vehicle' binds the subject: DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes the driver the one who drives or is in actual physical control of the vehicle, and the ontology reads 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds that vehicle, of the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. The mapping index maps the same words to the same atom."}, {"span": "ob1", "atoms": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic", "dev.stop_sign", "dev.yield_sign", "dev.governs", "kin.speed", "rel.occupies", "st.stop_line", "st.crosswalk", "st.entrance_of", "st.region_geometry", "st.travel_region", "st.lane_direction", "st.lane_enters", "st.intersection", "st.on_way", "st.highway", "st.sight_along_way", "prim.region_offset_along"], "derived": ["drv.motion.standstill", "drv.motion.region_entry"], "justification": "'shall stop' is the halt DEF-NRS-484A-255 defines, 'complete cessation from movement', carried by drv.motion.standstill within the speed tolerance its contract names; 'or yield', owed where the governing sign is a yield sign (dev.yield_sign, 'regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt', dev.stop_sign being the sign that requires the halt, dev.governs tying each to this approach), is carried by kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', at or below p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed at the place. The place is read in the words' own order: st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device', then st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', each tied to the subject's own entrance by st.entrance_of, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks ... the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before', with st.lane_enters giving 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', st.travel_region the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over and rel.occupies the anchor to the subject's own carrier; then the point at which st.sight_along_way, 'the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye at the observation ... the smaller of the two directions', reaches the view distance, on the way st.on_way and st.highway bind. prim.region_offset_along gives which side of the mark the subject is on along the carrier's designated direction st.lane_direction, and st.region_geometry the distance between the subject's body and the mark that the stop-point tolerance bounds; the primitive's own inputs are not claimed beside it. 'before entering the crosswalk', and the entry into the junction the act precedes, are the event drv.motion.region_entry denotes, 'comes to overlap a structure region at the observation'. 'approaching traffic' is DEF-NRS-484A-285's aggregate, claimed as the single atom ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic. st.sight_along_way is not a stand-in for whether an actual road user is seen (rel.visible): the words require a view of the way whether or not anyone is on it. st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line."}], "operationalizations": [], "assumptions": [], "intentions": [], "compositions": [], "residues": [], "binders": [{"name": "v", "class_elements": ["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}], "applicability": "The subject vehicle approaches an intersection -- it occupies a carrier whose entrance end is that junction -- and a stop sign or a yield sign governs that carrier. The event is the subject's entry into that intersection; the target is the approach carrier it occupies whose entrance end is that junction. The place is the stop line recorded as marking that carrier; where the carrier's stop lines are observed and none marks it, the crosswalk recorded as marking that carrier; where neither is marked, the point on that carrier nearest the junction at which the sight along the crossing way, in the lesser of its two directions, is at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance. The act counts at the place where the subject's speed is at or below p.standstill_speed_tolerance, or under a yield sign at or below p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed, while the distance between its body and the mark is at most p.stop_point_tolerance and it has not yet passed the mark, the side read by the sign of prim.region_offset_along along the carrier's designated direction; an act whose footprint already overlaps the junction is not at the place. The search runs back from the entry observation and ends at the start of that approach -- the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the mark marks, was off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance -- or at the subject's previous entry into the same junction, and at nothing else: not at another junction, not at the first observation of the recording, not at a distance travelled. Where the search finds the act the duty is met; where it reaches either end without it the duty is violated; where it reaches neither end, because the history begins before the recording or because the carrier's association with the mark or its direction is unobserved, the duty is unknown. Where a mark's entrances are observed and exclude the subject's carrier, the place is read from the next words in order and the duty is not unknown on that ground.", "params": ["p.standstill_speed_tolerance", "p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed", "p.stop_point_tolerance", "p.intersecting_way_view_distance"], "narrowings": [{"span": "ob1", "why": "'or yield' at a yield sign is read as the subject's speed at the place being at or below p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed -- the sign's own contract requires 'yielding without a mandatory halt' -- together with the precedence the next sentence states, which the second node of this line carries. A reading that demanded a halt under a yield sign would hold the subject to more than the words.", "kind": "reading"}, {"span": "ob1", "why": "'a clearly marked stop line' is read as the stop line the scene represents: the line's presence is the evidence of its clear marking, and the paint's clarity or wear is not modelled. The reading relaxes neither which place governs nor the act and its timing.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "status"}, {"span": "ob1", "why": "'the through highway' is read as the crossing highway at whose entrance the subject's governing stop or yield sign stands: DEF-NRS-484A-275 makes a through highway one at whose entrances traffic is required by law to yield in obedience to such a sign, and the sign governing this approach is the observable evidence of that designation.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "status"}, {"span": "ob1", "why": "'has a view of approaching traffic' is read as the sight along the crossing way reaching at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance in the lesser of its two directions, not as the driver's actual perception, which no trace carries.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "perception"}, {"span": "c1", "why": "'proper signs have been erected' is read as the presence on the road of a stop sign or a yield sign governing the subject's approach carrier: the feature's presence is the observable evidence of its proper erection by an authority.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "status"}, {"span": "s1", "why": "'the driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.", "kind": "observable_reading", "category": "agency"}], "scenarios": [{"name": "forbid", "expected": "violated", "narrative": "A side road meets a highway. A stop sign governs the car's approach lane, a stop line is recorded as marking that lane, and no officer or signal controls the junction. The car rolls over the line at 4 m/s and enters the junction, its speed never falling to the standstill tolerance anywhere on the approach from the line's upstream zone onward. No other road user is in the scene.", "masked": []}, {"name": "permit", "expected": "compliant", "narrative": "The same junction and stop sign. The car comes to rest with its speed at zero while its body is within the stop-point tolerance of the stop line and short of it, then enters the junction. The scene holds no other road user and the verdict is still decided.", "masked": []}, {"name": "idle", "expected": "not_applicable", "narrative": "The same geometry, but a police officer stands in the junction giving a proceed indication to the traffic on the car's approach.
